verdict.wording: FR: 'doit donner un préavis écrit d'au moins combien ?' is awkward because 'combien' has no noun. AR: 'ما الحد الأدنى للإخطار الكتابي' is elliptical, because the minimum is of a length of time, not of the notice itself. 'ما الحد الأدنى لمدة الإخطار الكتابي' is better. None of the three versions says the notice goes to the current employer, but they all leave it out in the same way, so the meaning stays the same.

The genitive 'كم يومٍ' is better than 'كم يومًا' after a noun in construct, although the accusative is also accepted. 'المرسوم بقانون اتحادي' is the correct official form. EN: 'the gratuity equals how many days of basic wage' is acceptable but loose. 'is calculated on the basis of how many days' basic wage' would be closer to the statute.

FR: putting the question inside the sentence («l'indemnité de fin de service correspond à combien de jours de salaire de base ?») sounds spoken, not legal. EN: 'the end-of-service gratuity equals how many days of basic wage' is a little loose. It is the gratuity for each such year, not the whole gratuity, that equals X days. Better: 'the end-of-service gratuity is calculated at how many days' basic wage'. This applies equally to all three versions and does not change the expected number.

verdict.problems: There is no real difference in meaning. All three versions name the same law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, as amended), ask about the same rule (the minimum age at which a person may be employed) and ask for the same unit (years). The Arabic 'الحد الأدنى لسن تشغيل الشخص' clearly refers to the worker's age. The EN 'minimum age for employing a person' and especially the FR 'l'âge minimum pour employer une personne' could also be read as the age the employer must have. This is unlikely to change the answer in practice, but the ambiguity is stronger in FR than in EN, and AR does not have it. One ambiguity is shared by all three versions: the law sets a general minimum working age and also has a separate juvenile category with conditions up to age 18. 'Minimum age for employing a person' could therefore point either to the absolute minimum or to the age of full, unrestricted employment. The intended answer is probably the absolute minimum, but no version says this explicitly.

A more natural wording is 'dans quel délai à compter de la fin de la relation de travail l'action fondée sur les droits prévus par cette loi doit-elle être introduite pour demeurer recevable ?'. 'à compter de' is the usual way to state a time limit, rather than 'après'. 'Recevable' is an acceptable equivalent of the Arabic notion of a claim not being heard (عدم سماع الدعوى), though it is not exact. AR: 'خلال كم سنة' is closer to everyday speech than to legal drafting. 'قبل أن يمتنع سماعها' is understandable but unusual. A native jurist would expect wording that follows the statute, for example 'ما المدة، بالسنوات، التي لا تُسمع بعد مضيّها من تاريخ انتهاء علاقة العمل الدعوى المتعلقة بأي من الحقوق المقرّرة في هذا المرسوم بقانون؟'. Also, 'قانون العمل الاتحادي' followed by 'هذا القانون' is loose: the instrument is a مرسوم بقانون (decree-law) on the regulation of labour relations, so 'هذا المرسوم بقانون' is more accurate. EN: 'within how many years ... before it can no longer be heard' is acceptable. 'from the date of termination of the employment relationship' would be closer to the statute's wording.

An English jurist would read 'working days' as jours ouvrés, which gives a different figure (25 per year, so about 2.08 a month, instead of 2.5).
